newsitem.title: USA: Arco earnings jump 52 percent in quarter.
newsitem.headline: Arco earnings jump 52 percent in quarter.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co. said Monday its earnings jumped 52 percent in the third quarter, fuelled by higher oil prices and natural gas production and improved results in its refining operations.

The nation's seventh largest oil company is the latest producer to report higher earnings fuelled by a jump in oil prices. But it was one of the few posting higher profits in refining, noting that strong product prices and increased volumes more than offset higher crude oil costs.

Los Angeles-based Arco also said it planned to buy convertible bonds in a planned public offering to double its stake in Zhenhai Refining and Chemical Co., one of China's largest oil refiners, to about 20 percent.
It said net earnings rose to $479 million, or $2.94 a share, in the quarter, from $315 million, or $1.93 a share, in the 1995 quarter.
Sales grew 20 percent to $5.15 billion from $4.28 billion.
A 20 percent rise in natural gas production coupled with higher crude oil prices boosted earnings by 146 percent in the oil and gas segment, Arco Chairman Mike Bowlin said in a statement.

Arco said its average price for crude oil rose to $16.10 a barrel in the latest quarter from $12.23 a barrel in the 1995 period. Domestic natural gas prices averaged $1.71 for 1,000 cubic feet, up from $1.25 per 1,000 feet a year ago.

Crude oil prices have been rising since July on strong demand, especially in the United States, and delays in new world supplies, including postponement of a U.N. plan for Iraq to export oil to buy food and medicine.
In other areas, Arco said transportation earnings fell 12 percent, coal earnings more than doubled, and profits from its 49.9 percent stake in Lyondell Petrochemical Co. fell 63 percent.

Other big producers reporting higher earnings recently included Phillips Petroleum Co., whose profits rose 38 percent, Texaco Inc., up 50 percent, Chevron Corp., which had a 29 percent gain excluding special items, and Exxon Corp., the nation's largest oil company, whose profits rose 4 percent.

Arco's results beat average forecasts for earnings of $2.60 a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates. Arco stock rose 62.5 cents to $133 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

It also said the Zhenhai Refining bonds it plans to buy would convert into stock giving it about 20 percent of the compay, up from 9.9 percent currently. The planned bond sale is subject to approval by shareholders and regulators, as well as other conditions, it noted.

Separately, Parker & Parsley Petroleum Co., Midland, Tex.-based oil and gas company, reported a third quarter profit of $21 million, or 58 cents a share, for the quarter, compared with a loss of $6.9 million, or 20 cents a share, in the same period in 1995.
